purpose: Research-only. Permit facts by river, quoted from the managing agency. Nothing was applied for, entered or submitted, and no agency was contacted.

salt-river-lower.passRequired: Tonto Pass (day-use fee) at Tonto day-use sites
salt-river-lower.agency: USDA Forest Service, Tonto NF (Mesa RD)
salt-river-lower.detail: No float permit. Tonto day-use sites need a Tonto Pass; some need a watercraft sticker (see the individual site pages). Check the site page before you go.

salt-river-upper.permitRequired: Mar 1 - May 15 (Tonto NF) + White Mountain Apache Tribe permit
salt-river-upper.agency: USDA Forest Service, Tonto NF + White Mountain Apache Tribe
salt-river-upper.quote: A Tonto National Forest Upper Salt River boater permit is required to float the Salt River Canyon Wilderness from March 1st to May 15th annually.
salt-river-upper.detail: Lottery; $16 application fee + $6 transaction fee; $125 boater permit fee if awarded (Tonto permit page). Motorized equipment and boats are prohibited in the Wilderness. A White Mountain Apache Tribe permit is also needed for the reservation stretch above the Wilderness.

dateConflict.note: The Tonto permit page and the Tonto permits page / Recreation.gov give different lottery opening dates. Not resolved; do not publish a lottery date.

verde-river-upper.note: No float permit statement on the Prescott NF Black Canyon / Bignotti pages or the Clarkdale Tuzigoot page.

verde-river-camp-verde.note: No float permit statement on the Prescott NF White Bridge / Clear Creek / Beasley Flat pages.

verde-river-scenic.quote: The group size on this section of river is limited to 25 people.

verde-river-wild.quote: Group size is limited to twelve people.
verde-river-wild.detail: Overnight trips on the Verde Wild and Scenic River need a fire pan and a portable toilet (Tonto order 03-04-06-23-25, Dec 1, 2023 - Dec 1, 2028).
verde-river-wild.orderQuote: without possessing an approved portable toilet and sewage containment system

verde-river-lower.note: Box Bar and Needle Rock are Tonto fee sites; no float permit.

gila-river-gila-box.note: No float permit or fee statement was found on the BLM Gila River Boat Put-In, Dry Canyon or Gila Box RNCA pages (the BLM charges fees at the two campgrounds only).
gila-river-gila-box.quote: We charge fees at both campgrounds.

colorado-river-grand-canyon.quote: Permits for these trips are made available to the public through a WEIGHTED LOTTERY
colorado-river-grand-canyon.detail: 12 to 25 day noncommercial trips from Lees Ferry. Lees Ferry is in Glen Canyon NRA; the launch is the start of the Grand Canyon permit.

colorado-river-lower-gorge.agency: NPS Grand Canyon NP + Hualapai Tribe
colorado-river-lower-gorge.quote: Grand Canyon National Park authorizes up to two noncommercial river trips to launch from Diamond Creek each day. Each trip is limited to a maximum of 16 participants.
colorado-river-lower-gorge.detail: Currently the National Park Service does not charge permit fees for this section of the river, but the Hualapai Tribe will charge access fees

notRequested: No permit, lottery entry or form was submitted. No agency or tribe was contacted.
